tools.name: list_services
tools.description: The services sold online with their unit, whether get_quote can price them, their "from" price in every currency (VAT included where it applies), the currencies, speeds and certifications get_quote accepts, the volume discount tiers and what counts as a page.

tools.name: list_languages
tools.description: The language codes get_quote and create_order accept, each with the country whose sworn translators serve the language.

tools.name: list_countries
tools.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes for country_of_use (where the translation will be used) and customer_country (where the customer is, which decides VAT), each with whether it is in the Hague Apostille Convention, whether sworn translations are offered for it, and whether document notarisation and ap

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: Where each service is available: the languages and certifications of certified translation and the countries whose authorities ask for each; the countries document notarisation and apostille & legalisation are offered for, with their routes, formats and turnaround, and whether each is priced online

tools.name: send_document
tools.description: Sends a document to be translated (PDF, image or Office file, up to 25 MB): a file the user attached in chat as `document`, a public https `url`, or `content_base64` with its filename when you hold the bytes yourself. It is measured the way the order form measures an upload; the response carries the

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: The price of a certified translation for a language pair, page count (or the documents sent with send_document), speed, certification and currency: the same calculator as checkout, with the ex-VAT lines, the VAT and the total, every certification the pair offers with its total, a delivery estimate a

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Places an unpaid order for the customer from the same arguments as get_quote plus their name, email and E.164 phone. The response carries signed links: pay_url is our payment page (card, PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay) to give the customer, status_url shows the order and collects any missing document

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Where an order stands, from its signed status_url: status, payment, balance due, due date, documents received, the next action (pay, upload_documents, wait) and fresh links. The link is the credential; nothing else identifies an order.

tools.name: recover_order_links
tools.description: Emails the customer fresh pay and status links for an order placed with their email address. The answer is the same whether or not the order and email match, so it reveals nothing about other people's orders.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_order · Private data: list_countries, get_coverage, send_document, get_quote, create_order, get_order_status · Public sink: send_document, create_order, recover_order_links.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_order · Private data: list_countries, get_coverage, send_document, get_quote, create_order, get_order_status · Public sink: send_document, create_order, recover_order_links

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
